Yamhill County Circuit Court

Introduction

The Yamhill County Circuit Court, part of Oregon’s judicial system, serves as a general jurisdiction court handling civil, criminal, family, juvenile, probate, and traffic cases. This guide provides detailed information on its operations, services, and resources.

History

Established in 1843 during the Oregon Territory era, the court has evolved significantly. Key milestones include the construction of its historic courthouse in the late 19th century and modernization efforts to meet growing community needs.

Structure & Jurisdiction

  • Departments: Civil, Criminal, Family Law, Juvenile, Probate, and Traffic.
  • Key Roles:
    • Clerk of the Court: Manages records, filings, and public assistance.
    • Jury Commissioner: Oversees jury selection and management.
  • Jurisdiction: Handles felonies, civil claims over $10,000, domestic relations, probate, and appeals from lower courts.

Court Services & Proceedings

  • Case Types:
    • Civil: Contract disputes, personal injury, etc.
    • Criminal: Misdemeanors and felonies.
    • Family Law: Divorce, custody, support.
    • Probate: Wills, estates, guardianships.
  • Jury Duty:
    • Eligibility: Residents 18+, U.S. citizens, no felony convictions (unless rights restored).
    • Process: Random selection via voter/license records. Exemptions available for hardship.
  • Filing Cases:
    • Online: Via Oregon’s eCourt system.
    • In-Person: Submit documents at the courthouse. Fees vary by case type.

Records & Access

  • Public Access: Most records are available online via OJCIN Case Search.
  • Fees: Copy costs vary (e.g., $0.25/page for standard documents). Certified copies require additional fees.
  • Restrictions: Sealed records (e.g., juvenile, sensitive family cases) require court approval.

Legal Resources

  • Attorneys: Contact the Oregon State Bar (503-684-3763) for referrals or pro-bono assistance.
  • Self-Help: The court provides forms and guides online. Visit the Oregon Judicial Department for resources.
  • Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR): Mediation/arbitration services available; contact the court for referrals.

Appeals Process

  • Grounds: Legal errors during trial, not new evidence.
  • Procedure: File a notice of appeal within 30 days of judgment. Consult an attorney for guidance.

Specialized Courts

  • Small Claims Court: Handles claims up to $10,000. No attorney representation allowed.
  • Municipal Court: Addresses city ordinance violations (e.g., traffic tickets). Separate from Circuit Court.

Community Outreach

  • Programs: Legal clinics, school outreach, and victim/witness assistance.
  • Accessibility: ADA-compliant facilities; request accommodations via court staff.

Contact & Directions

  • Phone: +1 503-434-7530 (Main)
  • Email: Yamhill.CircuitCourt@ojd.state.or.us
  • Parking: Available nearby; public transit routes serve the courthouse.

Future Developments

Planned upgrades include enhanced digital services (e-filing expansion) and facility improvements. Check the court’s website for updates.

FAQs

Q: How do I look up a case?
A: Use the OJCIN portal with case number or party name.

Q: Where do I get divorce records?
A: Certified copies from the court or Oregon Vital Records.

Q: Can I appeal a small claims decision?
A: Yes, to Circuit Court within 30 days.
